notes.title: Introducing Beef Cat Ultra!
notes.notes:
Introducing Beef Cat Ultra!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2796510/Beef_Cat_Ultra/

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2796510/Beef_Cat_Ultra/]BEEF CAT ULTRA WISHLIST PAGE[/url]

A retro-infused auto-shooter where you play as the titular Beef Cat and 5 of his friends. Battle the forces of Some Big Guy through 4 hand-crafted worlds across several gameplay styles like Survival, Collectathon, and Gauntlet (the like old game series that's sadly not continued anymore).

Watch the trailer and take it all in, we'll be discussing the game in much more detail as time goes on but let's meet the Beef Cat Team!

Our Media Creator is @thet.blahaman, Thomas Blaha, and put together this first teaser. He is also our certified Steam Deck play tester.

The rocking soundtrack is put together by @tacosaladninja, Andrew James Smith, which by-the-way, I sprung this entire project on him after recruiting him for Neon ClusterFx. Not only did he pivot, he's made all but one track for the BCU soundtrack already and it's a JAM of beeps, boops, and guitars.

And then me @clydefrog90210, Kyle Blaha, acting as sole Game Designer. But I can't take credit for a lot of the wonderful retro aesthetic art in the game, that credit goes to five different freelance artists in itch.io who will all be credited in-game.

Beef Cat Ultra releases this summer on Steam and you can wishlist it now!

notes.title: Patch 1.1
notes.notes:
[h1][b]Patch 1.1[/b][/h1]

[b][h2]A New Underground[/h2][/b]

We begin the journey to the depths of the patch notes with an overhauled underground experience. Starting small, a visual make-over has been done on the Frack Spots to make them less contrasting with the dirt and appear more visually palette-able. Small and subtle but effective.

Introducing Dense Dirt in the underground: this new underground tile has a gravel-y look and can be built through but pipes built through it will cost more monthly maintenance. A tutorial for Dense Dirt has been added to Scenario 2: Rocky Situation, and the tiles themselves have been added to more than a dozen stages throughout each mode.

Permafrost is re-freshed: building pipes through the icey permafrost tiles now shatters the ice while doing the same environmental damage as before. This is given a unique sound effect and animation and makes the tiles feel more special.

[b][h3]Introducing Gold Fracks[/h3][/b]

We are still technically talking about the underground. This is a new "mode" and victory condition. Scattered throughout the underground are eight Gold Frack Spots. Victory is simple, frack all eight spots and win. This is introduced in a tutorial in a new scenario, Scenario 12: Going for Gold. It has been added as a Quickplay option and every single quickplay stage is hand-made tailored to be compatible with the new victory condition. Adding new challenge to any stage.

[b][h3]Time to Excavate[/h3][/b]

Yes, we are *still* in the underground. The excavation tool has been entirely revamped. Selecting it in the Contractor Building now enters Excavation Mode - same as before. Hovering over a rock shows the cost to delete the block. That's not all though. Hovering over Dense Dirt and Permafrost also shows their excavation costs. Giving more player choice in how to navigate to underground - upfront costs or lasting effect?

[b][h2]Life As a CEO[/h2][/b]

The underground isn't the only place with significant new features. Try your hand in the financial sector with the new abilities - Government Bailout and Small Business Loan! You can take out a loan now, with interest of course. But you can also save yourself from financial failure with a crisp check from the government. With a collection of new financial abilities you'll probably want to make a build around them. So,

[b][h3]Introducing Amethyst Analytics[/h3][/b]

The sixth company in Frack the World is Amethyst Analytics and they are focused on the financial side of running a business. Their first Company Asset is pretty straight-forward: they start with more money than the other companies to get the wheels of changes going quickly. Their other Company Asset is tied to a new ability - the interest rate on small business loans is reduced. If you ever found yourself itching for more cash this may be your team. They do have an Oversight though - they consistently draw less oil from all Frack Spots than other companies because of their lack of expertise in actually, you know, fracking. 

[b][h3]Introducing Company Assets and Oversights[/h3][/b]

Maybe you caught that last paragraph if you've played a bunch. This is a large balance change. Company passive abilities have been re-branded as Company Assets. Along with this, every single company (kind of?) has one Oversight - the thing they kind of suck at. Ruby Fracking Co. - the darling protagonist of our fracking journey has no discernable oversight. The others aren't so lucky. Sapphire Drilling has higher pipe maintenance costs. Peridot Fabrications yields no oil from excavation. Etc etc.

[b][h2] And a Lot More[/h2][/b]

Look there is a ton in this patch - way more than I expected but also strangely not including a couple things I mentioned a few weeks ago. Some stuff as it turns out needs more time to cook. But the full patch notes are below and I've highlight key things not mentioned above. These are not organized particularly well and I think I would go nuts actually organizing them now.

If you've read this far and want to support the continued development of Frack the World - please leave a review on the Store Page! One review goes a long way in visibility. I'm loving patching and adding to this game and seeing any sort of engagement is just so highly motivating as a solo developer.

Thanks all, enjoy the game!
Kyle

notes.title: Fracking Milestone!
notes.notes:
I'm so happy to say over 500 of you have made Frack the World such a personal success!

I had written in my notebook prior to launch that I expected 50 people to play my game. Lofty goals. To be crossing the 500 player threshold a little over a month into the game's life is mind-blowing to me. So, thank you all - really.

Anyways, several weeks have passed since launch and 8 patches alongside it that have addressed dozens of quirks and quality of life things. Beyond that I was able to add a new company and scenario. It's the quality of life stuff that really makes me happy and I hope it's noticeable in-game.

I think that very must-address launch issues are out of the way at this point, and I'm looking ahead to a major patch. So let me give some teases as to what to expect.

Patch 1.08 will be the largest I've done so far, adding new content, further quality of life options, and tweaks to quirks that are discovered. I'm aiming for Late-May for this patch currently. Here's a quick idea of what you may find (certain things may of course change or be delayed to later patches):

-the sixth company, focused on economic builds, with perks associated with a new system
-a new system: government bailouts. With the economist hired and a reasonable payment to the right people, get a last ditch cash infusion when you would otherwise lose a match
-at least one new scenario introducing the new company, clearing this will unlock them in Quickplay
-a new Special Game Mode: Free Build - all of the systems of a Quickplay match with no costs. The environment can and will still deteriorate but you won't have to worry about going broke. A perfect place to practice or build a pipe masterpiece
-several new Quickplay stage layouts
-several additional Steam achievements

And that's all I'll lay out for now. Again, I'm aiming for Late-May and intend for everything above to be in Patch 1.08.

Thank you all for playing and hopefully I'll see you all again when the next patch and the next milestone is met!

-Kyle

notes.title: Frack the World is Available Now!
notes.notes:
[b]Frack the World[/b] is available now!

Wow. So I made a Reddit post this morning hoping to drive my expectation for 5 players up to 6. A sincere heartfelt thanks to the Reddit community for making this not only one of the most memorable days of my life - but leaving me totally speechless. As of writing this, my hope of 5 players has been far succeeded and there are over 100 people fracking the world. You have no idea what that means to me.

I have worked on this game for so long. I'm so proud of it. And I am so excited that so many people are playing it - even if it does kind of terrify me. Please please let me know if you stream the game, I will try to pop in. If you have any questions or feedback, don't hesitate to let me know. I want to listen to all feedback earnestly. 

I want to quickly make some context before the next bit. I am a solo developer with a full time work schedule and this is my first big release. I say this so that the pacing of patches to improve the game - which I'm insanely proud of - is set with realistic expectations. That said I've loved the feedback I've heard so far from people playing the game today while I was at work. Great stuff and stuff I take to heart.

I will have a hotfix made available within a week addressing three points of early feedback:
-an error with the volume setting not loading correctly when adjusting in prior sessions
-a visual queue to sell oil to help make the system more intuitive (its the S key)
-prevent the player from purchasing buildings when they don't have the funds (this was something I intentionally chose, but considering I've seen it several times in the early feedback, my intention was wrong and I will adjust it)

Thank you all for making this a day to remember, and frack away!
Kyle

notes.title: Frack the World Releases Wednesday March 1st!
notes.notes:
[b]Frack the World[/b], the first game from [b]Beef Cat[/b], launches [b]March 1st[/b]!

Before I get into [b]Frack the World[/b], which is already introduced in the game page, let me introduce myself. [b]Beef Cat[/b] is a small team of brothers making gaming content across streaming, YouTube, and game development - consisting of myself (Kyle) and my brothers (Thomas, Alex). We are all passionate about the game industry and all get different things out of it. Unified under the [b]Beef Cat[/b] umbrella we all get a place to express it.

[b]Frack the World[/b] is a solo dev game, made entirely by myself (Kyle) aside from some small things. Some early art assets were originally put together by another member of [b]Beef Cat[/b] but exist in the game now with large edits by me. The soundtrack is also not done by myself - instead using Royalty Free feel-good corporate tracks and lo-fi to drive home the satire of the game's concept.

This has been a work of passion for far longer than I'd like to admit and my first large foray into game development. I can't wait for everyone to check it out and I am insanely proud of where it is.

That said, I absolutely plan on supporting this game after launch with [i]small updates addressing any issues that may arise[/i], along with [i]larger updates adding new content[/i] to play around with. Sometime after launch, once I've figured out where the game stands, I will discuss my post-launch content plans. The game at-launch is what I consider a full experience that I would be happy with unchanged. Anything added to the game just adds to that value I think [b]Frack the World[/b] already has - a statement I hope you find yourself agreeing with.

This game has been a labor of love for a chunk of my life and that isn't changing. I will keep tinkering as long as I stay interested in the concept of the game - which I foresee being quite a bit of time. If you find yourself in a giving mood, please share the game page with friends, discords, etc and help make the launch an amazing day!

[u][b]Here's to a bold new step into the games industry - a dream come true and personal accomplishment I deeply cherish.
[/b][/u]
[i]See you on March 1st![/i]
-Kyle
